title: Cognito token purposes
storyboard: Compare ID token identity claims, access token API scopes, and refresh token renewal. Draw three distinct destinations: ID token → app identity display; access token → authorized API; refresh token → Cognito token endpoint → new ID/access tokens. Show refresh token opaque, ID/access JWTs. Do not imply every API accepts any token.
teachingClaim: ID, access and refresh tokens have distinct consumers and purposes.

title: ALB authentication session
storyboard: Sequence browser HTTPS request → ALB HTTPS listener → redirect to OIDC provider → authorization code returned to ALB → ALB exchanges code and retrieves claims → secure authentication cookie to browser → authenticated request to target with user claims. Show subsequent request reuses valid ALB cookie. No claim backend receives ID token.
teachingClaim: An ALB HTTPS authentication rule establishes a browser session before forwarding claims to targets.

title: Identity pool guest access
storyboard: Compare two request lanes: guest without IdP login → identity pool unauthenticated role → limited AWS credentials → read public app assets; signed-in user with IdP token → authenticated role → scoped AWS credentials → private user assets. Explicit guest access must be enabled. Roles/policies remain required in both lanes. No shared long-lived keys.
teachingClaim: Identity pool guest access must be enabled and uses its own scoped IAM role.

title: AppSync real-time subscriptions
storyboard: A client subscribes through AppSync persistent WebSocket; a second client performs a GraphQL mutation; the mutation triggers a matching subscription update to subscribers. Show server authorization before subscription. Small query vs mutation vs subscription comparison: read / change / receive updates. Do not show DynamoDB update alone automatically triggering a GraphQL subscription.
teachingClaim: A matching GraphQL mutation publishes real-time updates to authorized subscriptions.

title: Amplify end-to-end test gate

title: Scope IAM PassRole
storyboard: Caller creates a Lambda function with an existing execution role. Show separate gates: lambda:CreateFunction on function, iam:PassRole on approved execution role ARN, role trust for lambda.amazonaws.com. A compact condition label iam:PassedToService = lambda.amazonaws.com narrows the target service. Caller passes role; Lambda assumes role. Do not depict PassRole as caller assuming execution role.
teachingClaim: Creating a Lambda function, passing its execution role and trusting Lambda are separate permission checks.

title: Parameter policy actions
storyboard: Three rows under Advanced parameters: Expiration → delete parameter at configured time; ExpirationNotification → EventBridge event before/after expiry; NoChangeNotification → EventBridge event after unchanged interval. Route notification events to a configured SNS target rule. Clarify notification does not rotate the value. Compact timeline and actions, precise labels, no fabricated JSON.
teachingClaim: Advanced parameter policies can delete values or emit expiration and no-change events.

title: Choose a KMS encryption API
storyboard: Comparison table with visual paths: Encrypt sends small plaintext to KMS and returns ciphertext; GenerateDataKey returns plaintext data key plus encrypted copy for local data encryption; GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext returns only encrypted data key. Show data key in memory only, encrypted key stored with encrypted data. Do not imply KMS Encrypt accepts entire large files or that encrypted key can encrypt locally without decrypting.
teachingClaim: Choose Encrypt or a data-key operation according to where plaintext encryption occurs.
